format_note.es: Cada decisión es un Decision Trace explicable. No guardamos razonamiento privado del modelo: guardamos objetivo, contexto, restricciones, alternativas, decisión, justificación, consecuencia y estado.
format_note.en: Every decision is an explainable Decision Trace. We do not store a model's private reasoning: we store objective, context, constraints, alternatives, decision, justification, consequence and status.
format_note.pt: Cada decisão é um Decision Trace explicável. Não guardamos o raciocínio privado do modelo: guardamos objetivo, contexto, restrições, alternativas, decisão, justificativa, consequência e status.

objective.es: Decidir cómo organizar los datos del sistema para que nada se mezcle.
objective.en: Decide how to organize system data so that nothing gets mixed together.
objective.pt: Decidir como organizar os dados do sistema para que nada se misture.

decisions.context: The system must preserve history, allow analysis, produce reusable knowledge and expose an operational brain.
constraints: Must be inspectable by a human
Must not require a server to run

alternatives.rejected_because: Mixes interpretation with raw history; impossible to audit.

alternatives.option: One flat folder of markdown files
alternatives.rejected_because: Not queryable, no relations, no graph.

alternatives.option: Five separated levels: raw / processed / knowledge / project / control

decisions.decision: Five-level separation (raw, processed, knowledge, project, control).
decisions.justification: Raw stays immutable and auditable; processed can be regenerated; knowledge becomes reusable; control lets a new session avoid re-reading the universe.
decisions.consequence: The processed level can always be rebuilt from raw. Losing an index is never losing history.
decisions.evidence: Session where the architecture was defined by the user and validated against an empty repository.

objective.es: Elegir la base de datos y el motor de búsqueda del Knowledge Engine.
objective.en: Choose the database and search engine for the Knowledge Engine.
objective.pt: Escolher o banco de dados e o motor de busca do Knowledge Engine.

decisions.context: Node 22.22 ships node:sqlite natively. Verified in this sandbox: table creation, writes, reads and FTS5 MATCH queries all work with zero npm packages.
constraints: Must be able to evolve to PostgreSQL later

alternatives.rejected_because: No full-text search, no relations, O(n) scans.
Native compilation, install step, breaks offline-first.
Requires a running server; overkill for a local-first MVP.
Heavy dependency; semantic search can be added later as an adapter.

decisions.decision: node:sqlite (built into Node 22) + FTS5 virtual tables, with JSON files for configuration.
decisions.justification: Lowest initial complexity, real full-text search, local/offline operation, zero supply-chain risk.
decisions.consequence: The schema is portable SQL, so it can migrate to PostgreSQL later without redesign.
decisions.evidence: Executed probe: FTS5 OK, sqlite version 3.51.3.

objective.es: Decidir qué guardar del razonamiento de la IA.
objective.en: Decide what to store about the AI's reasoning.
objective.pt: Decidir o que guardar do raciocínio da IA.

decisions.context: The user asked to document reasoning. A literal transcription of a model's private reasoning is neither accessible nor useful.

alternatives.rejected_because: Not reliably available; noisy; not a learning artifact.
Loses the 'why', which is the whole point.

decisions.decision: Store Decision Traces: objective -> context used -> constraints -> alternatives considered -> decision -> justification -> action -> result -> verification -> learning.
decisions.justification: It is more useful than raw reasoning because it is structured, queryable and teachable.
decisions.consequence: The question 'why did we choose X?' becomes answerable by navigating decision -> searches -> sources -> comparison -> implementation -> result.
decisions.evidence: Decision Trace example #00421 in the architecture conversation.

decisions.context: The user called them 'Cortes'. They were informal notes about blocked work.
constraints: Must feed a Failure & Recovery Engine

alternatives.option: Keep them as free text notes
alternatives.rejected_because: Not queryable, not recoverable.

alternatives.option: First-class INTERRUPTION EVENT with typed taxonomy

decisions.decision: Interruptions become first-class events with types: blocked, failed, interrupted, waiting_user, dependency_missing, tool_error, ambiguity, conflict, resource_limit, security_stop, scope_change.
decisions.justification: A typed taxonomy allows automatic recovery planning and metrics on failure patterns.
decisions.consequence: Enables the Failure & Recovery Engine and the EVOLVE mode.
decisions.evidence: INTERRUPTION EVENT schema in the architecture conversation.

objective.es: Elegir el stack de la capa de aplicación.
objective.pt: Escolher o stack da camada de aplicação.

decisions.context: The user answered 'all three options' and demanded: full-featured AND fully offline.
constraints: Must work with no node_modules at all
Must also offer the full React/Next.js experience

alternatives.rejected_because: Requires npm install; not offline-capable from a clean clone.
Does not satisfy the requested full stack.

alternatives.option: Hybrid: zero-dep core + zero-dep console + Next.js app on the same API

decisions.decision: Hybrid three-layer front end: (1) core/api zero-dep HTTP server, (2) apps/console offline static UI served by it, (3) apps/web Next.js app consuming the identical API contract.
decisions.justification: The API contract becomes the seam. Offline capability is guaranteed by layer 1+2; full features by layer 3.
decisions.consequence: Any UI can be replaced without touching the engine.
decisions.evidence: User answer: 'Quiero una mezcla o seria hibrido... Seria una respuesta = Las 3.'

objective.es: Definir el idioma del código y de los comentarios.
objective.en: Define the language of code and comments.
objective.pt: Definir o idioma do código e dos comentários.

decisions.context: User: 'todo la creacion en ingles, los comentarios de los codigos en trilingue con explicacion total como si fuera un curso para recien iniciando en el lenguaje y programacion en si.'
constraints: Comments must teach programming itself, not just this project

alternatives.rejected_because: Contradicts the explicit trilingual teaching requirement.

alternatives.option: Manual translation of prose docs only
alternatives.rejected_because: Does not teach while reading code.

alternatives.option: English identifiers + trilingual pedagogical comment blocks (ES/EN/PT) with a BEGINNER COURSE section

decisions.decision: Identifiers, types and events in English. Every file carries a trilingual header and a BEGINNER COURSE block; key logic carries stacked ES/EN/PT inline comments.
decisions.justification: Reading the source becomes a programming course in three languages at once.
decisions.consequence: Files are longer. That is accepted deliberately: teaching value outweighs brevity.
decisions.evidence: User answer to the language question.

objective.es: Definir el alcance de la primera entrega real.
objective.en: Define the scope of the first real delivery.
objective.pt: Definir o escopo da primeira entrega real.

decisions.context: 32 sections of architecture existed but the repository contained only a 20-byte README.
constraints: Must not attempt 30 modules at once
Must leave a complete map for future sessions

alternatives.rejected_because: High risk of leaving everything half-finished.

alternatives.option: Build only the core with no structure
alternatives.rejected_because: Future sessions would have to redesign the layout.

alternatives.option: Complete physical skeleton of all 8 phases + phases 0-2 fully executable

decisions.decision: Full directory skeleton (section 25 of the architecture) with a SPEC.md per module, plus Phase 0 (Bootstrap), Phase 1 (Capture) and Phase 2 (Knowledge Engine) really implemented and tested.
decisions.justification: A new session can read the skeleton and know exactly what exists, what is stubbed and what to build next.
decisions.consequence: Phases 3-7 are documented stubs, not dead folders: each has an executable-shaped contract.

objective.es: Decidir cómo validar datos sin romper la regla de cero dependencias.
objective.en: Decide how to validate data without breaking the zero-dependency rule.
objective.pt: Decidir como validar dados sem quebrar a regra de zero dependências.

decisions.context: The original stack table listed Zod for validation. Zod is an npm package; POL-0005 forbids core dependencies.

alternatives.rejected_because: Violates the zero-dependency core policy.
Corrupt control files would silently break every session.

alternatives.option: Hand-written micro-validator with a chainable Zod-like API

decisions.decision: Implement core/validation/schema.js: a ~200-line chainable validator (z.string(), z.enum(), z.array(), z.object(), optional/default/parse/safeParse).
decisions.justification: Keeps the API shape familiar from Zod so swapping to the real Zod later is a one-line adapter change.
decisions.consequence: Validation covers the control plane; it is intentionally not a general-purpose schema library.

objective.es: Decidir el papel de LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, n8n, Dify, Flowise y Langflow.
objective.en: Decide the role of LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, n8n, Dify, Flowise and Langflow.
objective.pt: Decidir o papel de LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, n8n, Dify, Flowise e Langflow.

decisions.context: These frameworks were studied previously and are tempting to embed.
constraints: Must be replaceable without destroying the system

alternatives.option: Put them all inside the core
alternatives.rejected_because: Creates an unmaintainable monstrosity.
Throws away useful research.

alternatives.option: Optional adapters behind a stable interface

decisions.decision: External orchestrators are optional adapters only. The core ships its own orchestrator/planner/executor contract.
decisions.justification: Technology can change without destroying the system.
decisions.consequence: mcp/ and agents/ directories define adapter contracts, not implementations, in this phase.

objective.es: Elegir el runner de pruebas y el sistema de módulos.
objective.en: Choose the test runner and module system.
objective.pt: Escolher o runner de testes e o sistema de módulos.

decisions.context: Node 22 includes node:test and node:assert natively and supports ESM.

alternatives.rejected_because: npm dependencies.
Legacy syntax and no verification layer.

decisions.decision: ESM modules ("type": "module") with the built-in node:test runner and node:assert/strict.
decisions.justification: Verification exists from day one at zero cost, satisfying Layer 8.
decisions.consequence: Tests run with `npm test` or `node --test tests/`.

objective.es: Crear el repositorio separado develo-courseapp-simplify y abrir allí el PR.
objective.en: Create the separate develo-courseapp-simplify repository and open the PR there.
objective.pt: Criar o repositório separado develo-courseapp-simplify e abrir o PR nele.

decisions.context: The user asked for a second repository. The sandbox GitHub token is a limited integration.

alternatives.rejected_because: HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration (createRepository)'.
Violates traceability.

alternatives.option: Build in the session branch AND prepare a ready-to-push local repository /home/user/develo-courseapp-simplify with a simplify remote

decisions.decision: Mirror the work into a local git repository named develo-courseapp-simplify, pre-configured with per-phase commits and a remote placeholder, so the user only has to create the GitHub repo and push.
decisions.justification: Preserves the user's intent without inventing permissions we do not have.
decisions.consequence: One manual step remains for the human: create the GitHub repo (or grant permission) and run the provided push command.
decisions.evidence: gh repo create -> 403; git push --dry-run origin -> success.

objective.es: Entregar la aplicación utilizable en escritorio y móvil, con y sin conexión a internet, sin añadir dependencias.
objective.en: Deliver the application usable on desktop and mobile, with and without internet connection, without adding dependencies.
objective.pt: Entregar o aplicativo utilizável em desktop e celular, com e sem conexão com a internet, sem adicionar dependências.

decisions.context: The user asked for the app to work on desktop AND mobile, offline AND online (both modes). The console was already a zero-dependency web app served by genesis serve, but it was not installable and it died when the API was unreachable.
constraints: POL-0001: zero npm dependencies in the core, fully offline
No build step allowed for the offline console
One codebase must serve desktop and mobile
Stale data may be shown but must always be flagged as stale

alternatives.option: Electron desktop app + Cordova/Capacitor mobile wrapper
alternatives.rejected_because: Bundles Chromium/native toolchains and hundreds of npm packages; breaks POL-0001 and the empty-node_modules acceptance test, and triples repo size.
Requires a Rust toolchain on every machine that builds the app; the project must run on a bare Node 22 install.

alternatives.option: Plain website without service worker, showing "you are offline" when the API dies
alternatives.rejected_because: Fails the explicit requirement of being usable without connection; an error screen is not a mode.

alternatives.option: Installable PWA (manifest + service worker + bundled snapshot.json) with a three-tier data layer: live API -> service-worker cache -> snapshot

decisions.decision: Ship the console as an installable PWA: web manifest + generated PNG icons + service worker with per-resource cache strategies (cache-first shell, network-first API with last-good fallback) + a bundled snapshot.json so a never-connected install still opens with real data. One responsive codebase (drawer + bottom tabs on mobile, sidebar on desktop) covers both form factors. The UI always displays the active mode (live / cached / snapshot) and the sync time.
decisions.justification: A PWA is the only option that installs on desktop and mobile, works offline, keeps zero dependencies and needs no build step. The service worker turns "offline" from an error into a mode with real data, and the snapshot makes even the first offline boot useful.
decisions.consequence: apps/console gains sw.js, manifest.webmanifest, icons/ (generated by scripts/generate-icons.js) and snapshot.json (generated by scripts/export-console-snapshot.js). POL-0011 now forbids shipping a view that cannot render from cache or snapshot. Regenerating the snapshot is part of the release ritual.
decisions.evidence: curl: /manifest.webmanifest -> application/manifest+json; /sw.js -> no-cache; /snapshot.json -> 74 frozen API responses; icons are valid PNGs (192/512/maskable) produced by a dependency-free encoder.
